response.sql: WITH state_totals AS (SELECT c.state_county_province AS st, COALESCE(SUM(ft.transaction_amount), 0) AS total FROM Financial_Transactions ft JOIN Accounts a ON a.account_id = ft.account_id JOIN Customers c ON c.customer_id = a.customer_id GROUP BY c.state_county_province), shares AS (SELECT st, total, total * 1.0 / SUM(total) OVER () AS share FROM state_totals), with_avg AS (SELECT st, total, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM shares) SELECT SUM(total) AS combined_total, AVG(share) AS average_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_average_share FROM with_avg WHERE share > avg_share;

assumptions.assumption: A transaction is tied to a customer through Financial_Transactions.account_id -> Accounts.customer_id -> Customers. Inner joins drop transactions that have no matching account or customer.
Customers with a NULL state_county_province form one group, which is how GROUP BY treats NULLs. Empty-string states are kept as their own separate group and are not merged with NULL.
A state whose transactions all have NULL amounts still counts as a state, with a total of 0. It is included in the average of shares across states.
Each state's share is its total divided by the sum of all state totals. The average share is the unweighted mean of those shares across states.
